faq.question: Why does Homebridge warn that the `Name` or `Configured Name` characteristic exceeded the maximum length of 64?
faq.answer:
HomeKit enforces a hard limit of 64 characters on accessory and service `Name` and `Configured Name` characteristics.

The plugin automatically creates default names for auxiliary services and event switches by concatenating the appliance name with descriptive service labels (such as `[Appliance Name] Machine Care & Optional Filter`). If an appliance has a particularly long name in the Home Connect app, the combined service string can exceed 64 characters, causing HAP-NodeJS to log a validation warning.

To resolve this warning:
- Shorten the appliance name in the official Home Connect app.
- Alternatively, rename the individual service directly in the Apple Home app or Homebridge settings.
faq.semantic_abstract: HomeKit enforces a strict 64-character limit on `Name` and `Configured Name` characteristics, leading to validation warnings when composite service names built from appliance names and event descriptors exceed the length constraint.

faq.question: Why does renaming an appliance in the Home Connect app not update in Apple Home?
faq.answer:
Although the plugin synchronises appliance and service names from the Home Connect API on start-up, Apple Home prioritises user-defined names set within HomeKit.

If an accessory or service name has ever been edited directly in the Apple Home app, HomeKit stores that custom name override and ignores any subsequent name updates supplied by the plugin or the Home Connect platform.

To update the displayed name:
- Rename the accessory or service directly within the Apple Home app.
faq.semantic_abstract: Apple HomeKit preserves local user edits to accessory and service name characteristics, causing HomeKit to ignore upstream appliance name synchronisation from the Home Connect API once a name has been modified in the Home app.
